title: The Chiaroscuro All Stars date and short solos
summary: Wilson describes a recent date modeled on three-minute 1930s records with eight- and sixteen-bar solos.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, I work quite often with him at jazz festivals. Of course, recently up there in Colorado Springs, Gibson's party. And I did a record date I'm proud of called "Teddy Wilson's All Starts" for the Chiaroscuro label a couple years ago when he was on trumpet, and had Vic Dickinson on trombone and Bob Wilber on reeds. Bob, incidentally, did the little sketch arrangements this time. And Major Haley on bass and we had Oliver Jackson on drums. And we tried to do kind of like we did in the old days. We made three minute records, the guys stuck with eight bars, and 16. No extended solos, every tune was down to three minutes. We did the same format on this all-star date that we used to do back in the '30s.
You know, back in those days they played eight bar solos and it's a masterpiece, you could be heard
Yeah, they'll play you two hours. But, you know, the best solo Goodman ever made on record was the "Moonlight Can Do," it was only 16 bars.
